source_caption_text:
Pharrell’s reaction when Kanye played him “Through the Wire” for the first time

Before Kanye West became a household name as a solo artist, he was still trying to convince the industry that he could be more than just a producer. One person whose opinion mattered to him was Pharrell Williams. In the Jeen-Yuhs: A Kanye Trilogy documentary, Kanye plays Pharrell an early version of “Through the Wire,” giving him a chance to hear what he had been working on.

Pharrell is immediately drawn to the record, nodding along as Kanye’s vocals play over the Chaka Khan sample. But once Kanye explains that he recorded the song with his jaw wired shut following his near-fatal car accident, Pharrell is visibly taken aback. He even steps out of the room for a moment before returning to tell Kanye how much he loves the track.

The exchange is memorable because Kanye was sharing a record that would become one of the defining songs of his early career with someone he genuinely looked up to. Pharrell’s reaction and encouragement meant a lot, especially at a time when Kanye was still fighting for recognition as a rapper.
